## Purpose

Penguin Explorer helps undergraduate biology students investigate:

**How do body mass and flipper length differ among Adelie,
Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins, and how do these comparisons change
when viewing males and females separately?**

## Install the package

Run these commands in your R console:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-jlii0673-coder"
)
```

## Launch the app

```{r launch, eval=FALSE}
library(exploredata)
launch_app()
```

The app opens locally and uses data included in the installed package.
An internet connection is not needed to retrieve data when it runs.

## Use the controls

1. Keep all three species selected to compare their distributions.
2. Change the sex selection from All to Male, then Female.
3. Observe how the points, sample counts and summary means change.
4. Select two species to examine their overlap more closely.

All includes penguins with unknown sex. Male and Female include
only records with the selected recorded sex.

If you deselect every species, the app displays
"Please select at least one species."
Select a species again to restore the outputs.

## Read the outputs

Each point in the scatterplot represents one penguin:

- The horizontal axis shows flipper length in millimetres.
- The vertical axis shows body mass in grams.
- Colour identifies species.

Points toward the upper right represent heavier penguins with longer
flippers. Overlapping colours indicate similar measurements among
individuals of different species.

The table reports the number of selected records, complete records
and excluded records for each species. Both means use only records
with body mass and flipper length available. These are also the
records displayed in the scatterplot.

## Explore the summary function

The app uses the exported function `summarise_penguins()`.
You can also use it directly:

```{r overall-summary}
library(exploredata)

summarise_penguins(penguin_data)
```

In the full sample, Gentoo penguins have a mean body mass of
approximately 5,076 g and a mean flipper length of 217.2 mm.
Both means are greater than those of the other two species.

However, a group mean does not show all individual variation.
Use the scatterplot to examine overlap and spread.

To investigate the question within males:

```{r male-summary}
male_data <- penguin_data[
  !is.na(penguin_data$sex) & penguin_data$sex == "Male",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

summarise_penguins(male_data)
```

Repeat this comparison for females using the app.
Check whether the ordering of species remains the same and whether
the sizes of the differences change.

## Missing data and limitations

The prepared data contain 344 records. Two lack one or both
measurements, leaving 342 complete records in the overall plot
and summary means.

Filtering by sex also excludes records with unknown sex.
Always read the selected and excluded record counts alongside
the results.

The data describe sampled penguins from the Palmer Archipelago.
Species have unequal sample sizes, and the sample does not
necessarily represent other places or penguin populations.

The comparisons are descriptive. An association between flipper
length and body mass does not establish a causal relationship.

## Data source and preparation

The data originate from `palmerpenguins::penguins_raw`, made available
by Dr Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station LTER under CC0.

See the [Palmer Penguins documentation](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/)
for source and citation information.

The repository script `data-raw/prepare_penguins.R` selects relevant
fields, standardises names and sex labels, retains missing values,
checks the prepared data and saves the package dataset.
